topic: Why traffic jams appear out of nowhere

through_line.name: red brake lights
through_line.progression: one car's brake lights flick on, then the follower's flare harder, then a whole column glows red, then the red band slides backwards on the chart
through_line.resolution: behind the smooth driver the brake lights go dark and traffic flows

blocks.vo_line: This enormous traffic jam has no cause. Drive to its very front and you'll find no accident, no roadwork, just cars accelerating away.
blocks.through_line_state: every car in the jam shows red brake lights
shots: WIDE high overhead: three clay lanes packed with stalled sand-beige clay cars, every one with glowing red brake lights, slow push-in
CU low angle: a stopped sand-beige car's tail lights flick red with a stamp
MEDIUM lateral tracking: the camera glides past the queue toward the jam's front
ECU top-down: two stopped sand-beige cars sit nose to tail, the rear car's brake lights glowing red
MEDIUM high angle: at the front the blue car pulls away onto empty road and settles
blocks.audio: soft clay squish as the camera pushes in, a low toy-engine hum bed, a soft brake squeak, a quick whoosh as the blue car pulls away
blocks.direction_note: Every car in the jam is sand-beige; the cobalt-blue car is the only blue car. All cars face the same way and only move forward.

blocks.vo_line: In two thousand eight, Japanese researchers placed twenty-two cars on a circular track and instructed drivers to cruise at thirty kilometres per hour.
blocks.through_line_state: no red yet: every car cruises evenly, brake lights off
shots: WIDE overhead: clay cars slide onto a circular clay track one after another
MEDIUM low angle: evenly spaced cars roll past the inner curb
CU lateral: the blue car rolls steadily, its wheels turning
ECU macro: a sand-beige car's front wheel rolls steadily past the cream inner curb
MEDIUM high angle: the whole ring circulates smoothly, then settles into rhythm
blocks.audio: soft clay pops as cars drop onto the track one by one, a steady toy-engine hum bed, light ticking of turning wheels

blocks.vo_line: Smooth driving lasted only briefly, because whenever one motorist eased off slightly, the follower behind reacted late and braked noticeably harder.
blocks.through_line_state: brake lights flare red down the line of cars
shots: CU lateral: the blue car eases off and a gap opens ahead of it
MEDIUM low angle: the sand-beige car behind closes in fast
ECU rear view: the sand-beige car's brake lights flare red with a hard stamp
MEDIUM top-down: behind the sand-beige car a second sand-beige car's brake lights flare red even brighter
WIDE high angle: the trackside curve shows the cars bunching, then holds steady
blocks.audio: a short squeaky brake scrape, a whoosh as the gap opens, a firm clay thud as the brake lights flare
blocks.direction_note: All cars face the same way and only move forward.

blocks.vo_line: Every following driver braked a little harder, so one tiny wobble kept gradually amplifying until it became a complete stop-and-go traffic wave.
blocks.through_line_state: every brake light in the column glows red
shots: WIDE lateral: a long column of clay cars, all pointing the same way, rolls forward along a single clay lane
CU rear view from behind the column: tail lights flare red one after another, each a beat later, as each car slows
ECU top-down: the gaps between bumpers shrink as the cars bunch up nose to tail
MEDIUM low angle from the roadside: the last car rolls forward, nose first, and jolts to a full stop with a bump
WIDE high overhead: the whole column stands still with every brake light glowing red, then settles
blocks.audio: rolling toy-engine rumble bed, quick ticks on each tail-light flare, a soft squeak of brakes, a bump thud on the full stop
blocks.direction_note: Every car faces the same direction and only ever moves forward (nose first). No car ever reverses or moves backwards.

blocks.vo_line: Here's the surprise: the wave travels backwards, and on real highways jams drift upstream at roughly fifteen to twenty kilometres an hour.
blocks.through_line_state: the red clay strip slides backwards down the chart while the car tokens move forwards
shots: WIDE overhead: clay car tokens slide upward along grooved clay lanes
CU top-down: the red clay strip curls and slides downward, against the cars
MEDIUM low angle: a clay arrow pointing backwards stamps onto the clay board
ECU macro: the clay strip's edge creeps backwards across the grid lines
MEDIUM high angle: cars climb as the red clay band sinks, then everything settles
blocks.audio: soft sliding clay sounds as tokens climb, a slow sticky clay stretch as the strip slides back, a clay thud as the arrow lands

blocks.vo_line: Later experiments showed one smoothly driven car can calm these waves, so the jam's only cause, and cure, might be you.
blocks.through_line_state: no brake lights glowing anywhere: traffic flows
shots: MEDIUM low lateral: the lavender car cruises steadily forward with a wide empty gap ahead of it
CU high angle: the long empty stretch of asphalt between the lavender car and the car ahead
ECU rear view: the lavender car's brake lights stay dark as it coasts smoothly forward
MEDIUM roadside: sand-beige cars behind it flow evenly past the camera, brake lights off
WIDE high angle: the whole highway moves freely forward and settles into a calm final frame
blocks.audio: calm toy-engine hum bed, a gentle whoosh of flowing cars, a soft settling click at the end
blocks.direction_note: The lavender car is the smooth driver and is clearly visible in shots 1-3. All cars face the same way and only move forward.

overlays.text:
ONE SMOOTH DRIVER
CAN *CALM* THE WAVE
